Package com.github.crittscott.somestacks.gametest

Class ProtectionApiGameTests

java.lang.Object
com.github.crittscott.somestacks.gametest.ProtectionApiGameTests
All Implemented Interfaces:
net.fabricmc.fabric.api.gametest.v1.FabricGameTest
public final class ProtectionApiGameTests extends Object implements net.fabricmc.fabric.api.gametest.v1.FabricGameTest
Provider-backed checks, loaded only in development runs started with -PwithCommonProtectionApi=true. A test provider denies the positions a scenario names and records who asked and what stood there when it did.

    • automationGrowthConsultsProtectionApi

      public void automationGrowthConsultsProtectionApi(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      To reproduce in-game: deny [SomeStacks] placement in a claim managed through Common Protection API, then pipe items into a full Storage pile whose top sits under the claim. Growth accepts nothing, the input keeps its items, and no block appears.

      public void adjacentDepositConsultsProtectionApi(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)

    • automationCleanupConsultsProtectionApi

      public void automationCleanupConsultsProtectionApi(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      To reproduce: allow placement and interaction in a Common Protection API claim, but deny breaking for [SomeStacks]. Empty a temporary Storage Stack through a hopper; its empty block remains. Next allow the API query but deny breaking through a Fabric event listener; it still remains. Allow both and empty it again; cleanup removes it and emits destruction. The test verifies one cancellation on either denial and the original actor/state/entity.

    • playerCleanupConsultsProtectionApi

      public void playerCleanupConsultsProtectionApi(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      To reproduce: allow placement and interaction in a Common Protection API claim, but deny breaking for your player. Extract the last item from a temporary Storage Stack; its empty block remains. Repeat with the API allowing breaks and a Fabric listener denying them; it still remains. Allow both and empty it again; cleanup removes it as your player. The test checks callback context and destruction vibrations for all three cases.
